approach: Root cause: reading acceptance (`refusing_check`, crates/athena-core/src/reading/checks.rs:520-551) is an ordered list of `step!` checks and none compares the request's explicit parts with the reading's deliverables and criteria. No rule says an explicit part stays in scope unless the request defers it, so a reading that moves part (3) to `out_of_scope` is accepted (jobs 20261029-084645-sza7 and 20261029-110953-bw7k). Fix it at that gate with `check_request_parts`, placed last so every existing refusal keeps its refusing check. A new parser `request_parts` in topics.rs reads `N.`, `N)`, `(N)`, `a)`, `(a)` line parts, inline `(1)..(2)..` sequences, and `-`/`*`/`N.` bullets after an `Acceptance:` line; it skips quoted-evidence lines of generated root-cause requests. Coverage is judged on DISTINCTIVE stems only, so sibling parts that share a subject cannot cover each other. Revision, round 3 findings: (1) a function-word stop list is added, 3-letter stems match exactly only, prefix matching needs a shorter stem of 4+ chars, and the worked stem sets are recomputed under the rule exactly as stated and pinned by a unit test; (2) a stem that occurs in every part of its kind is dropped before matching, so the 'flag' subject shared by parts (1)-(3) cannot cover part (3), and the fixture keeps 'flag' in all three parts on purpose; (3) criteria are filtered by a broader negation list, a criterion that cites a part's marker AND holds a deferral word never covers it, and a marker citation covers only with one shared distinctive stem; (4) the tension between false refusals and misses is named, acceptance bullets are matched leniently (one distinctive stem), and a local proxy test runs the check over generated-request corpus cases; (5) run/pin.rs:167 is in dependents; (6) a sibling corpus helper takes the prevention text and still builds through `hestia::root_cause_request`; (7) the doc comment and CHANGELOG say why giving the reader the parts is not enough, and name passing the parsed parts to the reader as a follow-up. No prompt, config or record is edited.

decisions.choice: Add a new parser `request_parts(text) -> Vec<RequestPart {marker, kind, text, span}>` in topics.rs (kind = Enumerated or Bullet); leave `request_text_acceptance` and `is_bullet` unchanged. Skip quoted-evidence lines: those starting 'Introspection ', 'Cause:', 'Failure class:' or 'Priority:' and those holding 'prevention it proposed:'. Read inline `(1)..(2)..` sequences only from the remaining lines, only when every marker is followed by text with a significant stem, and end the last part at the first '. ' or line end.
decisions.reason: `request_text_acceptance` is the parse `athena plan` uses (topics.rs:276, plan_entry 411) and is called by steward.rs:587/1566/1582/1658, hestia.rs:1781 and code_health.rs:1348, and the corpus pins its bullet counts (refusal_corpus.rs:2788-2794) and 0 for `N)` and `(a)` parts. Generated root-cause requests quote each proposal on a line starting 'Introspection {id} (job {job}); prevention it proposed: ...' (hestia.rs:1041); an enumeration inside a quoted proposal must not become required parts, because the root-cause default lets the reader fix the cause another way.

rejected.why: Moves plan acceptance of every queued request and the pinned bullet counts.

rejected.option: Read inline sequences from the whole request
rejected.why: A quoted proposal with text after each marker would be required as parts.

decisions.reason: The new step runs only when every other check passes, so each existing Refuse case keeps its refusing check; `an_extra_check_with_no_case_is_reported` anchors on the `check_reading_references` step line (refusal_corpus.rs:2927) and still works. Only Accept cases with explicit parts can change.

rejected.why: It would pre-empt `check_outcome_state` in the delivery cases that carry `2)` and `(a)` parts (refusal_corpus.rs:936-949).

decisions.choice: Count enumerated parts anywhere (outside skipped lines). Count `-`, `*` and `N.` bullets only after a line equal to `Acceptance:` (case-insensitive).
decisions.reason: The failure class is a dropped enumerated part such as (3); acceptance bullets are the second introspection's proposal. Many tests run the real gate with short dash-bullet requests (reading.rs:2638, 2753, 2951; drain.rs:3988, 4067, 6320; job_plan.rs:166) and a free-form dash bullet is not a named part.

rejected.option: Treat every dash or star bullet as a part
rejected.why: Larger blast radius over fixtures the planner cannot run; false refusals on reworded bullets.
Leaves out the acceptance bullets that criterion 3 and introspection 20261029-111141-1661 name.

decisions.choice: Stems (`part_stems`): strip a leading `[tag]` of a criterion; lowercase ASCII alphanumeric words; drop all-digit words, words under 3 letters, `FUNCTION_WORDS` (the, and, for, not, with, are, its, can, all, any, one, add, use, new, via, per, but, has, how, out, was, may, our, you, see, two, who, why, too, now), `COMMON_WORDS` (topics.rs:157-161, all 4+ letters) and `PART_FILLER` (pass, cargo, clippy, fmt, content, behavior); drop a trailing `s` when the word is longer than 3; cut to 6 chars; map the stem `doc` to `docume` (`STEM_ALIASES`, so 'docs' and 'document' agree). `stems_match(a, b)`: equal, or the shorter has 4+ chars and is a prefix of the other. 3-letter stems match exactly only.
decisions.reason: Answers finding 1. COMMON_WORDS was written for `topic_words`, which keeps only 4+ letter words (topics.rs:170), so 'the', 'and', 'for' would survive as stems and make coverage almost free. Worked sets under this exact rule: (1) 'Add the --json flag to status' = {json, flag, statu}; (2) 'Document the flag in the guide' = {docume, flag, guide}; (3) 'Cover the flag with a timeout test' = {cover, flag, timeou, test}; criterion '[content] docs/guide.md describes --json' = {docume (alias of doc), guide, descri, json}. The unit test `part_stems_worked_examples` asserts these sets, so the numbers are measured, not assumed.

rejected.why: 'the' or 'not' would match 'then', 'note' and the like (finding 1).

rejected.option: Drop the alias and require 4-letter stems
rejected.why: The natural criterion 'docs/guide.md describes --json' would share only 'guide' with part (2) and be falsely refused.

decisions.choice: Coverage uses DISTINCTIVE stems. For each kind (Enumerated, Bullet) with 2+ parts, drop from every part the stems that occur in every part of that kind; if that empties a part, fall back to its full stem set. Let n be the part's remaining stem count. A part is covered when (a) one criterion, pooled with the stems of every deliverable path whose text the criterion contains, shares at least need stems with the part, or (b) one deliverable path alone (split on non-alphanumerics) shares that many, or (c) a criterion cites the part's marker (`(N)`, `part N`, `item N`, `(c)`, `part c`; not bare `N)`) and shares at least 1 distinctive stem. need = min(2, n) for Enumerated parts and min(1, n) for Bullet parts. `out_of_scope` never covers. A part with n = 0 is skipped.
decisions.reason: Answers findings 2 and 4. Parts of one request share a subject: in the fixture 'flag' is in all three parts, so a criterion for part (2) such as 'the guide documents the flag' ({guide, docume, flag}) would share 'flag' with part (3). With 'flag' dropped, part (3) keeps {cover, timeou, test} and that criterion shares none of them, so part (3) stays uncovered and the main demonstration refuses on real wording. Bullets are reworded more often and nearly every steward, hestia and code_health request ends in an `Acceptance:` section (steward.rs:581-585; replay reads the newest 50 accepted readings, replay.rs:142-157), so bullets need one distinctive stem. The tension is named: a stricter matcher refuses more reworded readings, a looser one misses dropped parts; the replay holds a candidate whose newly refused share exceeds the declared 10% plus the 5-point margin, 15% (replay.rs:296-308). The 10% is an estimate, not measured, because `records/` is absent.

rejected.option: Assign each criterion to the one part it best matches
rejected.why: More logic and tie rules; dropping stems shared by all parts fixes the stated failure with one rule.

rejected.option: Hand-tune corpus wording until cases pass
rejected.why: Hides the sibling-subject gap; the fixture keeps 'flag' in all three parts on purpose and a unit test pins the stem sets.

rejected.option: Count shared words across the whole reading text
rejected.why: Summary and title echo the request, so a dropped part would look covered.

decisions.choice: Criterion-side negation has three tiers. `DEFER_PHRASES` (narrow, job scope): follow-up job, follow up job, in a follow-up, in a follow up, as a follow-up, as a follow up, separate job, next job, later job, not in this job, deferred to, can wait. `CRITERION_NEGATION` = DEFER_PHRASES plus out of scope, out-of-scope, deferred, not done, not covered, skipped, left out, omitted, excluded, postponed, not part of. `MARKER_NEGATION` = CRITERION_NEGATION plus bare later, defer, skip, follow-up, follow up, followup, for now. A criterion holding any CRITERION_NEGATION phrase covers nothing. A criterion that cites a part's marker and holds any MARKER_NEGATION phrase does not cover that part. Matching is by `has_phrase` (surveys.rs:39) on lowercase text.
decisions.reason: Answers finding 3. After the refusal the reader gets one re-read (reading.rs:738-759) and could defer part (3) again with a criterion 'Part (3) is out of scope for this job' or 'Item 3 is deferred'. Bare 'later' stays out of CRITERION_NEGATION so a covering criterion 'Later retries reuse the cache' still counts for a part that it does not cite by marker; once a criterion cites the marker, bare 'later' is a deferral signal, because a false hit then costs one cover.

rejected.why: Leaves 'out of scope' and 'deferred' criteria as a way to defer on the re-read.

rejected.option: Bare 'later' and 'defer' in the list for all criteria
rejected.why: Refuses good criteria such as 'Later retries reuse the cache' and '(3) Defer the flush until exit'.

decisions.choice: The request defers a part only on a job-scope phrase: its own text, or another request sentence outside every part span and skipped line that holds a `DEFER_PHRASES` phrase and cites the marker as `(N)`, `N)`, `part N`, `item N` (letters: `(c)`, `part c`, `item c`). Bare later, future, for now, separately, defer and out of scope do not defer a part of the request. Part spans are blanked before the request is split on newlines and '. '.
decisions.reason: Brief criterion 4: refuse 'unless the request text itself defers it'. Ordinary parts like '(2) Reject future timestamps', '(1) List each file separately' and '(3) Defer the flush until exit' must stay required. A sentence 'Part 3 can wait for a follow-up job.' is the request deferring. The list is a known limit; a deferral worded otherwise is refused and the error text gives the repair.

rejected.option: Check only the part's own text
rejected.why: Refuses a reading that follows a request deferring the part in a later sentence.

decisions.choice: Enforce by code only, and say in the doc comment and CHANGELOG why giving the reader information is not enough: the reader already sees the whole request and still deferred part (3) in jobs 20261029-084645-sza7 and 20261029-110953-bw7k, so the root-cause policy's allowance for a refusal rule (hestia.rs:1017-1022) applies. Name 'pass the parsed request parts to the reader in its brief' as a follow-up, not part of this job. No prompt is edited (reader budget 1998 of 2000, docs/system-facts.md).
decisions.reason: Answers finding 7. The refusal text reaches the reader on its corrected re-read (reading.rs:738-759), which is the information channel that needs no new prompt tokens.

rejected.option: Add a rule line to the reader prompt
rejected.why: No token headroom, and prose is not a mechanism.

rejected.option: Build the parsed parts into the reader brief now
rejected.why: A larger change across briefs and budgets; stated as a follow-up.

risks.risk: False refusals of good readings that reword a part so it shares too few distinctive stems with any criterion. Stricter matching (needed to stop sibling parts covering each other) refuses more reworded readings; looser matching misses dropped parts.
risks.mitigation: The tension is named in the doc comment. Bullets need only one distinctive stem; parts with no stems are skipped; PART_FILLER and the gate words are filtered; a marker-citing criterion with one distinctive stem covers; stems pool one criterion with the paths it names; the error names the part and the repair and the reader gets one re-read (reading.rs:738-759). The proxy test over generated-request shapes guards the common case. The 10% is declared as an estimate; Athena's replay measures it at verification and the planner cannot (no `records/`).

risks.risk: Dropping stems that occur in every part leaves a part with few stems, so a vague criterion covers it, or a part with n=0 is skipped.
risks.mitigation: If the drop empties a part, fall back to its full stem set; need = min(2, n). Skipping an all-shared part is a known limit stated in the doc comment; the corpus has a narrowed-part case.

risks.risk: An existing scripted or stored reading with an `Acceptance:` section or enumerated markers is newly refused, forcing edits outside the five listed files (reading.rs:7396, 7743; steward.rs:2585-2639; run/tests.rs; drain.rs).
risks.mitigation: Dash bullets count only after an `Acceptance:` line and the search found no enumerated markers in requests outside the corpus. The producer runs `cargo test --locked`, `cargo test -p athena-core steward::tests`, `cargo test -p athena-core run::` and `cargo test -p athena-cli --test drain`, repairs the fixture's criteria, never the check, and names the file in the report.

risks.risk: Enumerations in quoted evidence of generated root-cause requests, or a marker list in prose ('such as (1), (2) and (3)'), are read as parts.
risks.mitigation: Quoted-evidence lines are never parsed; an inline sequence counts only when every marker has text with a significant stem. Cases `request-parts-quoted-proposal-enumeration-ignored` and `request-parts-marker-list-without-text` pin both.

risks.risk: The narrow request-side deferral list misses a real deferral worded another way, so a reading that follows the request is refused; the criterion-side lists may reject a legitimate criterion that says 'skipped' or 'omitted'.
risks.mitigation: The refusal text says the request itself must defer the part; the re-read can cover it. A criterion-side false hit costs one cover, not a required part. Stated as a known limit in the doc comment.

risks.risk: The recorded request text of jobs sza7 and bw7k is not in the snapshot, so the corpus shapes are rebuilt from the introspections' account.
risks.mitigation: The case `source` strings say 'rebuilt from the introspection's account', not 'verbatim'; the unit tests hold the property for any part (3), not one job.

risks.risk: The producer tunes corpus wording until cases pass and hides a matcher gap.
risks.mitigation: Stem sets are pinned by `part_stems_worked_examples`; if a case's stem count differs from the plan, the producer reports it and fixes the rule or the case with the pinned set shown, and never lowers a threshold silently.

demonstrations.method: Unit test in reading.rs. Request: 'Do three things:' with '(1) Add the --json flag to status', '(2) Document the flag in the guide', '(3) Cover the flag with a timeout test', once inline and once as separate lines. All three parts name 'flag' on purpose. Base reading from `terms_reading` (reading.rs:7293, wraps `governed_reading` 4635) with deliverables src/status.rs and docs/guide.md and criteria '[behavior] status --json prints json' and '[content] docs/guide.md documents the flag'. (a) part 3 absent: `refuser_for(&reading, request)` (reading.rs:7288) returns `Some("check_request_parts")`; this also shows a criterion written for part 2 does not cover part 3 through the shared 'flag'. (b) part 3 named only in `out_of_scope` as a follow-up: same. (c) added criterion '[behavior] a test fails when the timeout is missing' (stems test, timeou): `refuser_for` is None and `check_reading_acceptance` is Ok. (d) '(2) Reject future timestamps' dropped: refused. (e) same reading with criterion 'Later retries reject future timestamps': accepted. (f) criterion 'Part (3) is out of scope for this job' added to (a): still refused. (g) criterion 'Part (3) timeout test will be added later' added to (a): still refused (marker plus bare 'later'). A sibling test `part_stems_worked_examples` asserts the stem sets {json, flag, statu}, {docume, flag, guide}, {cover, flag, timeou, test}, {docume, guide, descri, json} and the distinctive sets after dropping 'flag'.
demonstrations.command: cargo test -p athena-core reading::tests::request_parts_refused_when_part_three_is_left_out && cargo test -p athena-core reading::tests::part_stems_worked_examples
demonstrations.observes: The refusing check is exactly `check_request_parts` for (a), (b), (d), (f), (g); the reading is accepted for (c) and (e); the stem sets equal the stated ones.
demonstrations.fails_without: With the `step!(check_request_parts(...))` line removed, `refuser_for` returns None for (a), (b), (d), (f), (g) and `assert_eq!(.., Some("check_request_parts"))` fails.
demonstrations.seam: Production entry points `refusing_check` and `check_reading_acceptance` through the existing helper `refuser_for` (reading.rs:7288); fixtures `terms_reading` and `governed_reading` exist. Nothing is faked and the check logic is not in the fixture. `part_stems` and `stems_match` are `pub(super)` in topics.rs so the test calls them directly. Tests added by plan step 5.

demonstrations.method: Unit test in reading.rs. On the part-three-moved-to-out_of_scope reading of criterion 2, `check_request_parts(..).unwrap_err().to_string()` contains the marker '(3)', 'timeout test', the cause 'out_of_scope' or 'follow-up', the repair 'deliverable and a criterion' and the exemption 'request itself defers'. A request whose part reads '(3) Add a dashboard in a follow-up job', and a request with '(1)..(3)' followed by 'Part 3 can wait for a follow-up job.', each with a reading that omits part 3: `check_reading_acceptance` is Ok. Parts '(3) Add a latest-value column', '(3) Reject future timestamps', '(3) Defer the flush until exit' and '(3) List each file separately' are NOT deferred: a reading that omits them is refused.
demonstrations.observes: The refusal names the part and the repair; a job-scope deferral in the request, in the part or a later sentence, is accepted; words that merely resemble deferral do not defer.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the check, `unwrap_err()` panics because the check is absent or returns Ok, so the first assertion fails.
